chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from one of our companions, from Salih ibn Umar, from Al-Hasan ibn Abdullah, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:
Do not seek assistance from the lazy one, nor should you consult an incapable one.

key_terms.عَاجِز: Incapable person; one who lacks ability or power
key_terms.كَسْلَان: Lazy person; one who is sluggish or indolent

ai.seo_question: What are the two types of people one should avoid seeking help or advice from according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this concise maxim from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to highlight the practical wisdom of delegating tasks to those with both the will and capacity to execute them. This teaching underscores the Shia ethical emphasis on *kafa'ah* (competence) and *ijad* (readiness), warning that associating with the lazy or incapable not only leads to failure but also reflects poorly on the leader’s judgment. It serves as a foundational principle for effective leadership and social organization in Islamic governance.
